scout:
**SCOUT DISPATCH — Wed 4 Nov 2026, 06:25 GMT**

**Lead: Democrats win the midterms, and the AI trade takes the first hit.**
- 
Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.2% overnight, S&P 500 futures were off 1.3% and Dow futures down 0.8%.

- 
CNBC reports that traders are betting the result will slow data-center buildout.
 
It also flagged that a Texas governor result raised data-center risks.

- 
The selloff came on a night when several big tech companies reported excellent earnings.
 Read it as political and policy repricing, not an earnings problem.
- Not confirmed: the size of the final Senate and House margins, and any specific policy path on power, permitting or AI. Expect a gap-down open, then a test of whether chips hold.

**AI-hardware earnings were strong after the bell (Tue 3 Nov).**
- AMD: 
revenue rose 45% to $13.38B and adjusted EPS was $2.09, against $1.95 expected.
 
Q4 guidance is about $17B.
 
Lisa Su said 2027 revenue could grow more than 80%.
 
The shares jumped nearly 9% after hours, then narrowed to about 4% as futures sank.

- Arista (ANET): 
revenue grew 58.5% to $3.66B.
 
Q4 guidance of $3.9–4.0B compares with about $3.6B expected.
 After-hours gains ranged from about 10% to 15%.
- Super Micro: 
fiscal 2027 sales guidance of $72–82B is above the $69.17B consensus.

- Skyworks: 
fell 17.4% on weak handsets.
 That is a read-through for the phone supply chain.
- Apple: 
flagged that rising memory costs are squeezing gross margins and that memory prices will keep climbing into next year.
 The shares fell. This is good for MU, SNDK, Samsung and SK Hynix, and bad for hardware margins.

**Chips went through a bear-market scare and bounced.**
- 
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq snapped a three-day losing streak on Tuesday, up 0.4% and 0.8%.
 
The Dow fell more than 0.4%.

- 
The rally was narrow. Most stocks fell as money left defensive names, and strong hiring data pushed yields up.

- 
South Korea stocks fell more than 5% as tech heavyweights followed Wall Street's AI-linked names lower.
 Samsung and SK Hynix are the exposure to watch.
- Friday 30 Oct was a heavy tech selloff. 
Headlines blamed AI costs and Fed speakers keeping hikes in play.


**Hyperscaler capex is now judged on cash flow.**
- 
Alphabet's capex surge to $51B pushed free cash flow to negative $9B for a second straight quarter. Microsoft generated $19B of positive free cash flow on similar spending.
 
Alphabet fell 11%.

- 
Microsoft trimmed its capex forecast to $170B from $175B, and Alphabet held at $195–205B.
 
Microsoft's CFO said third-party AI chip delays push some capacity into the first half of 2027.

- 
Meta guided full-year capex to $135–145B.

- 
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon all closed lower after their reports, with investors focused on cash burn.
 Sources conflict on Microsoft: one says 
investors cheered the report
, another says it ended the session flat. Treat Microsoft as roughly neutral to slightly positive.
- 
Hyperscaler capex is expected to top $1 trillion next year.
 That is the bull case for the suppliers. The risk is financing: 
CoreWeave's bond yields spiked, raising concern about debt-heavy neoclouds.


**Fed: a hiking regime, not a cutting one.**
- 
On 28 Oct the Fed held at 3.75%–4%.
 
Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack dissented, both wanting a quarter-point hike.

- 
Markets price one more 25bp hike in 2026, with further hikes into 2027.
 
Barclays sees hikes in December and January.

- Chair Warsh 
said he doesn't believe in forward guidance absent a crisis.
 That means more data-dependent volatility around each release.
- Next dates: 
minutes of the 28 Oct meeting on 18 Nov at 2:00 pm
, and 
the next decision on Wed 9 Dec.


**Rates, oil and Iran.**
- 
The US 2-year yield fell about five basis points to 4.566%, and the 10-year fell about six to 4.90%
 in early Wednesday trading.
- 
The 10-year touched 5.18% earlier in the cycle, its highest since 2007.
 The date of that peak is not confirmed in my sources.
- 
Oil fell for a second session on hopes of a diplomatic end to the eight-month conflict.
 Brent was around $101–104, WTI mid-$90s. Prices are volatile and headline-driven, and an earlier report put Brent as high as $117 on fears of renewed US strikes.
- Oil and yields are the swing factor for inflation. 
The September hike was driven by oil-fuelled inflation.
 A deal is bullish for duration, airlines, consumers and chips. A collapse in talks is the reverse. Energy names (XOM, COP, CNQ, BP, SHEL) trade the other way.
- Today's Treasury refunding announcement: 
Treasury sets out planned auction sizes for notes and bonds.
 Any shift in long-end supply moves long yields.

**Next two weeks: what matters most**
- **Today, 4 Nov:** ISM services (consensus 54.8). Earnings: ARM, QCOM (both after close, and both are AI/handset reads after the Skyworks miss and Apple's memory-cost warning), UBER, MCD, CVS, NVO, MCK, TM. 
CVS also moved after hours.
 I did not confirm the direction.
- **5 Nov:** SONY, COP, CNQ, PH report. Oil direction is the key for COP and CNQ.
- **6 Nov:** Jobs report (consensus 63K), and BRK.B earnings. Strong hiring data lifted yields on Tuesday, so a beat points to hike pricing and pressure on long-duration tech.
- **10 Nov:** CPI is the biggest macro event before December. It will decide whether the December hike is priced in.
- **11 Nov:** CSCO. **12 Nov:** AMAT, a read on equipment demand after the memory-price signals.
- **13 Nov:** PPI. Japanese banks MUFG, SMFG and MFG report.
- **17 Nov:** Retail sales. **NVDA after the close** is the big one. HD, DIS, BHP, PDD and MDT also report that day.
- **18 Nov:** PANW, LOW, TJX, plus the FOMC minutes. **19 Nov:** WMT.
- **24–25 Nov:** BABA, DELL, ADI, then DE.

**Positioning and sentiment**
- Sentiment is fragile and flips fast on headlines. 
Trader Tom Sosnoff argued the chip declines may be "just the beginning."
 
Melius cut its Nvidia price target.

- The other side of that view: 
Morgan Stanley strategists say the US correction is nearing an end
, and 
Nvidia is pushing faster AI-factory deployment.
 I did not confirm either call's detail.
- Not confirmed: fund-flow and options-positioning data. I found no hard numbers.

**What the council should hold in mind**
- Demand is not the problem. AMD, Arista and Super Micro all guided well above consensus. The questions are financing, power and policy, and rates. The election raises the odds of friction on data centers and energy.
- Hold the AI infrastructure names with pricing power. In memory, that means MU, SNDK and Samsung and SK Hynix. In networking and AI compute, that means ANET, AMD, AVGO and NVDA.
- Be wary of cash-burners without matching cash flow, and of rate-sensitive long-duration names if CPI is hot.
- The next hard test is CPI on 10 Nov, then NVDA on 17 Nov.

redteam.statement: The consensus is not diversified; it is two crowded trades wearing different labels. CB, MCK, BRK-B, ABBV, LLY, V, PGR, LIN and JNJ are about 40% of the book. Most sit 7-29% above their 200-day averages, with RSI of 65-79. Low beta measures the past. Anchor and Pulse said it themselves: they mean-revert together if defensives rotate out. The other half is ANET, ETN, MU, TSM, AMD and NVDA, one financing factor, now 18-20%. Add Democratic-Congress policy risk on pharma, distribution and interchange, and you have two policy factors, not hedges. Also, 27-34% cash earns about 4% but forfeits a rebound if CPI is cool. The plan is sound on dated triggers; it is fragile on correlation.

MCK is capped at 3% because it reports tonight after a 13% surge and has thin margins. ABBV is capped at 3% for pharma-pricing policy risk. LLY is capped at 4% at RSI 79. MU is capped at 3.5% at beta 3.4 with CXMT competing. ANET and ETN are capped at 5% each; they share one hyperscaler-financing factor. concerns: Cool CPI on Nov 10 could rotate money out of crowded defensives (CB, BRK-B, LLY, PGR, LIN) that mostly sit 7-29% above their 200-day averages.
ANET, ETN, MU, TSM, AMD and NVDA are one hyperscaler-financing and policy factor; the combined AI sleeve should stay near or below 20%.
A Democratic Congress adds policy risk to pharma, distributors, card interchange and data-center power at the same time.
Oil hedges (XOM, SHEL, COP) fail in an Iran settlement; the CEO warns oil could fall 40%.

chairRaw.statement: The council will hold a 70% invested book with 30% cash. About 20% sits in AI infrastructure at reset prices, and the ballast is spread across several drivers rather than one crowded defensive trade. Three arguments carried this. events.text:
**Scout dispatch, Wed 4 Nov 2026, 06:25 GMT**

**Lead: the market is wobbling on AI-spending doubts while the Fed leans toward hiking.**

**Last 7 days**
- **Fed (Oct 28):** 
The Fed held rates in a 10-2 vote.
 
Two of the 12 voters backed a hike.
 That follows 
a September hike, the first since 2023.
 Bond traders still see more hikes ahead (the Bloomberg/Yahoo snippet was cut off, so I couldn't confirm the details). Easing is not the base case.
- **Tape:** 
Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October.
 
The S&P 500 lost 0.9% and the Dow gained 1.7%.
 
Money rotated toward healthcare and other defensives.
 
AI spending doubts are weighing on risk assets.

- **Big Tech mixed:**
  - Alphabet (GOOG) 
missed on both top and bottom lines, which is rare.

  - Microsoft (MSFT) reported 
EPS of $4.89 on $92.28B revenue.
 I couldn't confirm the stock reaction.
  - 
Apple (AAPL) ended Tuesday's session about $94B below Monday's market value.
 Palantir (PLTR) and Shopify (SHOP) also fell Tuesday morning.
  - Oracle (ORCL) jumped on Oct 28, but I couldn't confirm why.
- **AI hardware is the bright spot:**
  - 
AMD's data center sales rose 97% to $8.5B.
 AMD was up about 8% after hours.
  - 
Arista (ANET) revenue grew 58.5%, its fastest since the IPO.

  - 
Astera Labs revenue rose 154%, led by AI switch chips.

  - 
Super Micro reported $19.9B in sales.

  - 
Shopify revenue grew 32%.

  - Chips lifted the Nasdaq on Tuesday.
- **Booking (BKNG):** 
Its results showed a $900M revenue cut tied to the FTC.
 I couldn't confirm the details.
- **Pfizer (PFE):** 
Shares slipped despite an earnings beat and a higher outlook.

- **Oil:** Prices fell on Iran deal hopes. That helps consumers and hurts energy names (XOM, CVX, COP, CNQ, PBR). I couldn't confirm the size of the move.
- **Politics:** Midterms were held Tuesday. 
TheStreet's headline said they favored Democrats.
 
JPMorgan expects modest market moves.
 Futures turned lower as results came in. Final control of the House and Senate is unconfirmed as of this writing.
- **Earnings backdrop:** 
FactSet has Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth at 30.2%, up from 29.5% a week earlier.
 Earnings are strong while price action is weak.

**Next 2 weeks (dates as supplied)**
- **Today, Nov 4:**
  - ISM services is expected at 54.8.
  - Before the open: CVS, MCD, NVO, UBER.
  - After the close: ARM, QCOM, MCK.
  - TM also reports.
  - ARM and QCOM matter most after AMD's strong print. Watch for AI-edge and handset commentary.
- **Thu, Nov 5:** CNQ, COP, PH and SONY report before the open. Oil's drop makes the energy guidance the one to watch.
- **Fri, Nov 6:**
  - The jobs report is the key event. 
Dow Jones consensus is 55,000. Your calendar shows 63K.

  - 
September was 29,000, against 88,000 expected.

  - A strong number raises December hike odds and hurts long-duration tech. A weak one helped tech rally in October.
  - BRK.B also reports.
- **Tue, Nov 10:** CPI. This is the second big print for hike pricing. PBR reports after the close.
- **Wed, Nov 11:** CSCO reports.
- **Thu, Nov 12:** AMAT reports after the close. It is a read on chip equipment demand.
- **Fri, Nov 13:** PPI. MUFG, MFG and SMFG report.
- **Tue, Nov 17:**
  - Retail sales.
  - NVDA reports after the close. It is the event of the window, and with AI doubts live, the guidance matters more than the beat.
  - HD and DIS report before the open. BHP, MDT and PDD also report.
- **Wed, Nov 18:** LOW and TJX report before the open. PANW reports.
- **Thu, Nov 19:** WMT reports before the open.
- **Nov 24–25:** BABA, ADI and DELL on the 24th, DE on the 25th.
- **Not on your list:** I couldn't confirm the date of the December FOMC.

**Sentiment and positioning**
- Sentiment is split. Defensives and value are winning. The AI trade is being sorted into suppliers with hard revenue (AMD, ANET, Astera, SMCI) and platforms or software with spending questions (GOOG, PLTR, SHOP, AAPL).
- 
A Schwab macro head called a tech downturn a possibly healthy reset.

- The rate backdrop is awkward. A weak jobs number was good for stocks in October, but sticky inflation caps the upside.
- I found no reliable data on fund flows or positioning, and I couldn't confirm any.

**What this means for The Future**
Hold what is being built for the future, which is AI infrastructure with demonstrated revenue. Be wary of crowded, long-duration names ahead of the Nov 6 payrolls, the Nov 10 CPI and NVDA on Nov 17. The Fed is more likely to hike than cut, so the macro risk is on the downside.

**SCOUT DISPATCH — Wed 4 Nov 2026, 06:25 GMT**

**Lead: Democrats win the midterms, and the AI trade takes the first hit.**
- 
Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.2% overnight, S&P 500 futures were off 1.3% and Dow futures down 0.8%.

- 
CNBC reports that traders are betting the result will slow data-center buildout.
 
It also flagged that a Texas governor result raised data-center risks.

- 
The selloff came on a night when several big tech companies reported excellent earnings.
 Read it as political and policy repricing, not an earnings problem.
- Not confirmed: the size of the final Senate and House margins, and any specific policy path on power, permitting or AI. Expect a gap-down open, then a test of whether chips hold.

**AI-hardware earnings were strong after the bell (Tue 3 Nov).**
- AMD: 
revenue rose 45% to $13.38B and adjusted EPS was $2.09, against $1.95 expected.
 
Q4 guidance is about $17B.
 
Lisa Su said 2027 revenue could grow more than 80%.
 
The shares jumped nearly 9% after hours, then narrowed to about 4% as futures sank.

- Arista (ANET): 
revenue grew 58.5% to $3.66B.
 
Q4 guidance of $3.9–4.0B compares with about $3.6B expected.
 After-hours gains ranged from about 10% to 15%.
- Super Micro: 
fiscal 2027 sales guidance of $72–82B is above the $69.17B consensus.

- Skyworks: 
fell 17.4% on weak handsets.
 That is a read-through for the phone supply chain.
- Apple: 
flagged that rising memory costs are squeezing gross margins and that memory prices will keep climbing into next year.
 The shares fell. This is good for MU, SNDK, Samsung and SK Hynix, and bad for hardware margins.

**Chips went through a bear-market scare and bounced.**
- 
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq snapped a three-day losing streak on Tuesday, up 0.4% and 0.8%.
 
The Dow fell more than 0.4%.

- 
The rally was narrow. Most stocks fell as money left defensive names, and strong hiring data pushed yields up.

- 
South Korea stocks fell more than 5% as tech heavyweights followed Wall Street's AI-linked names lower.
 Samsung and SK Hynix are the exposure to watch.
- Friday 30 Oct was a heavy tech selloff. 
Headlines blamed AI costs and Fed speakers keeping hikes in play.


**Hyperscaler capex is now judged on cash flow.**
- 
Alphabet's capex surge to $51B pushed free cash flow to negative $9B for a second straight quarter. Microsoft generated $19B of positive free cash flow on similar spending.
 
Alphabet fell 11%.

- 
Microsoft trimmed its capex forecast to $170B from $175B, and Alphabet held at $195–205B.
 
Microsoft's CFO said third-party AI chip delays push some capacity into the first half of 2027.

- 
Meta guided full-year capex to $135–145B.

- 
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon all closed lower after their reports, with investors focused on cash burn.
 Sources conflict on Microsoft: one says 
investors cheered the report
, another says it ended the session flat. Treat Microsoft as roughly neutral to slightly positive.
- 
Hyperscaler capex is expected to top $1 trillion next year.
 That is the bull case for the suppliers. The risk is financing: 
CoreWeave's bond yields spiked, raising concern about debt-heavy neoclouds.


**Fed: a hiking regime, not a cutting one.**
- 
On 28 Oct the Fed held at 3.75%–4%.
 
Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack dissented, both wanting a quarter-point hike.

- 
Markets price one more 25bp hike in 2026, with further hikes into 2027.
 
Barclays sees hikes in December and January.

- Chair Warsh 
said he doesn't believe in forward guidance absent a crisis.
 That means more data-dependent volatility around each release.
- Next dates: 
minutes of the 28 Oct meeting on 18 Nov at 2:00 pm
, and 
the next decision on Wed 9 Dec.


**Rates, oil and Iran.**
- 
The US 2-year yield fell about five basis points to 4.566%, and the 10-year fell about six to 4.90%
 in early Wednesday trading.
- 
The 10-year touched 5.18% earlier in the cycle, its highest since 2007.
 The date of that peak is not confirmed in my sources.
- 
Oil fell for a second session on hopes of a diplomatic end to the eight-month conflict.
 Brent was around $101–104, WTI mid-$90s. Prices are volatile and headline-driven, and an earlier report put Brent as high as $117 on fears of renewed US strikes.
- Oil and yields are the swing factor for inflation. 
The September hike was driven by oil-fuelled inflation.
 A deal is bullish for duration, airlines, consumers and chips. A collapse in talks is the reverse. Energy names (XOM, COP, CNQ, BP, SHEL) trade the other way.
- Today's Treasury refunding announcement: 
Treasury sets out planned auction sizes for notes and bonds.
 Any shift in long-end supply moves long yields.

**Next two weeks: what matters most**
- **Today, 4 Nov:** ISM services (consensus 54.8). Earnings: ARM, QCOM (both after close, and both are AI/handset reads after the Skyworks miss and Apple's memory-cost warning), UBER, MCD, CVS, NVO, MCK, TM. 
CVS also moved after hours.
 I did not confirm the direction.
- **5 Nov:** SONY, COP, CNQ, PH report. Oil direction is the key for COP and CNQ.
- **6 Nov:** Jobs report (consensus 63K), and BRK.B earnings. Strong hiring data lifted yields on Tuesday, so a beat points to hike pricing and pressure on long-duration tech.
- **10 Nov:** CPI is the biggest macro event before December. It will decide whether the December hike is priced in.
- **11 Nov:** CSCO. **12 Nov:** AMAT, a read on equipment demand after the memory-price signals.
- **13 Nov:** PPI. Japanese banks MUFG, SMFG and MFG report.
- **17 Nov:** Retail sales. **NVDA after the close** is the big one. HD, DIS, BHP, PDD and MDT also report that day.
- **18 Nov:** PANW, LOW, TJX, plus the FOMC minutes. **19 Nov:** WMT.
- **24–25 Nov:** BABA, DELL, ADI, then DE.

**Positioning and sentiment**
- Sentiment is fragile and flips fast on headlines. 
Trader Tom Sosnoff argued the chip declines may be "just the beginning."
 
Melius cut its Nvidia price target.

- The other side of that view: 
Morgan Stanley strategists say the US correction is nearing an end
, and 
Nvidia is pushing faster AI-factory deployment.
 I did not confirm either call's detail.
- Not confirmed: fund-flow and options-positioning data. I found no hard numbers.

**What the council should hold in mind**
- Demand is not the problem. AMD, Arista and Super Micro all guided well above consensus. The questions are financing, power and policy, and rates. The election raises the odds of friction on data centers and energy.
- Hold the AI infrastructure names with pricing power. In memory, that means MU, SNDK and Samsung and SK Hynix. In networking and AI compute, that means ANET, AMD, AVGO and NVDA.
- Be wary of cash-burners without matching cash flow, and of rate-sensitive long-duration names if CPI is hot.
- The next hard test is CPI on 10 Nov, then NVDA on 17 Nov.

final.statement: The council will hold a 70% invested book with 30% cash. About 20% sits in AI infrastructure at reset prices, and the ballast is spread across several drivers rather than one crowded defensive trade. Three arguments carried this. First, demand is proven while price has reset: ANET guided $3.9-4.0B against roughly $3.6B expected, and ETN's backlog is up 46%. The future this council exists to own is being sold on politics, not results. Second, the red team is right that the defensives mean-revert together, so every one is held at or under the risk caps. Third, CPI on 10 November is a dated fork, and cash funds either branch. I overrule the full exit from defensives and the 36% cash stance. MCK is excluded because it reports tonight after a 13% surge. My bias is consensus, and I have not paid for headcount.
final.summary: Own the physical bottlenecks of the AI buildout (networking, power, memory, foundry) and the cash-funded platform (MSFT), sized as one financing factor near 20%. Balance them with capped, uncorrelated ballast: insurance float, gases, payments, pharma and a small oil hedge. Keep 30% cash to redeploy after CPI on 10 November and NVDA on 17 November.
